claude-opus-4-5.instinct: Shapes deliverables to look polished regardless of underlying accuracy
claude-opus-4-5.typical_failure_mode: Recategorizes failures as manageable polish; can rate broken docs highly
claude-opus-4-5.planning_note: Produces a plan that reads thoroughly while quietly adding unneeded dependencies

claude-opus-4-6.instinct: Makes reasoning inspectable; leaves the audit trail visible
claude-opus-4-6.planning_note: Most readable plan in panel — forensic instinct produces prose a new engineer can follow

claude-opus-4-7.instinct: Asks what standard or process would make a defect impossible
claude-opus-4-7.planning_note: Only model to consistently close each phase with testable exit conditions

claude-opus-4-8.instinct: Reads spec and source in parallel, grounds every edit in documented requirements
claude-opus-4-8.typical_failure_mode: Over-reads and re-validates; assumes environment tools exist before checking
claude-opus-4-8.planning_note: Inherits governance instinct from Opus 4.7 lineage; strongest on spec-anchored tasks with clear oracles

claude-sonnet-4-5.instinct: Scores, grades, gates, and percentage-tables whether asked or not
claude-sonnet-4-5.typical_failure_mode: Can over-credit visible structure; calibration gaps under open-ended prompts
claude-sonnet-4-5.planning_note: Highest form-consistency but shakier precision under the presentation

claude-sonnet-4-6.instinct: Shrinks the distance between a finding and a fix
claude-sonnet-4-6.risk_tolerance: Low (most willing to call something broken)
claude-sonnet-4-6.typical_failure_mode: May skip root-cause strategy in favor of immediate fix
claude-sonnet-4-6.planning_note: Makes operationally risky things structurally impossible via CI/drift detection

claude-sonnet-5.instinct: Refuses to declare done until the real oracle passes; reconstructs broken verification paths
claude-sonnet-5.typical_failure_mode: Verbose output; may over-explain during execution
claude-sonnet-5.planning_note: Strong recovery from broken commands; will reverse-engineer the intended test if the prescribed path fails

openai-gpt-5.2.instinct: Compresses risk into the fewest useful decisions
openai-gpt-5.2.planning_note: Catches mechanical failures others soften (--max-warnings 0, exit-code discipline)

openai-gpt-5.4.instinct: Reframes messy work into a coherent system
openai-gpt-5.4.planning_note: Most valuable when input is ambiguous; least valuable when already tightly specified

anti_patterns.name: False confidence pipeline
anti_patterns.description: Pairing Sonnet 4.5 with Opus 4.5 as your only reviewers. Both produce polished, reassuring outputs with documented calibration gaps. Together they create a pipeline where two models agree things are fine while concrete failures go unflagged.
anti_patterns.fix: Always include at least one low-risk-tolerance model in correctness-critical loops: Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6, or GPT-5.2.

anti_patterns.name: Redundant insight loop
anti_patterns.description: Using two Opus models in the same review loop expecting diverse insight. Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.7 produced verbatim-level score and fix duplication in structured review — they converge on verdict even though their personalities differ.
anti_patterns.fix: Cross the family line whenever possible. A better pairing crosses the optimism spectrum: one cataloguer, one systems thinker, one pragmatic operator.

anti_patterns.name: Executor without verifier
anti_patterns.description: Using a surgical executor (Sonnet 4.6) without a verification step. Its instinct is to fix immediately, which can skip root-cause analysis. The fix may be correct but the underlying problem recurs.
anti_patterns.fix: Pair executors with a verifier pass: Sonnet 5 (refuses to declare done until oracle passes) or Opus 4.8 (spec-driven validation) as a post-execution check.
